Description: Before dinner begins, Annie Beaumont and Helen Dauer have a probing conversation in the Living room about the stolen pocket watch. Annie repeatedly contradicts herself and is explicitly marked as lying by the narrator, while a suspicious “stranger” trying to go to the Chapel is introduced as a lead.
Location: Living room（Living room）
Key Information:
  - The conversation occurs before dinner begins, in the Living room (Living room).
  - Annie Beaumont proactively tells Helen Dauer she may know where the pocket watch is.
  - Helen Dauer confirms for the first time in this node that the pocket watch has indeed been stolen, and she shows clear regret.
  - Helen Dauer says she acquired the pocket watch not long ago and wasn’t sure why she bought it at the time.
  - Helen Dauer says several people in the house have been acting strangely, and mentions she just saw a funny-looking male stranger in the Living room.
  - The stranger said late at night that he wanted to go to the Chapel (Chapel), which Helen Dauer considers suspicious.
  - Annie Beaumont says Tony Dauer once mentioned a name written on the pocket watch’s box, but she does not elaborate.
  - Annie Beaumont changes her story, saying she only saw someone carrying the pocket watch out of Helen Dauer’s room but didn’t see who it was.
  - The narrator explicitly labels Annie Beaumont’s pocket-watch-related account as an obvious lie.
  - Helen Dauer mentions her daughter has not explained what happened that day to her.
  - Helen Dauer suggests they should go to the Dining room and judges dinner will be ready soon.
Characters:
  [Annie Beaumont（Annie Beaumont）] Person No. 2.
    · Proactively tells Helen Dauer she may know the pocket watch’s whereabouts.
    · Contradicts herself repeatedly—first implying she has a lead, then backtracking.
    · Claims she saw someone carry the pocket watch out of Helen Dauer’s room but does not identify who.
    · Her key statements about the pocket watch are explicitly judged as lies by the narrator.
  [Helen Dauer（Helen Dauer）] Person No. 9.
    · Confirms the pocket watch was stolen.
    · Says the pocket watch was bought not long ago.
    · Mentions a suspicious male stranger who tried to go to the Chapel at night.
    · Expresses disappointment that her daughter has not explained what happened that day.
    · Suggests going to the Dining room, judging dinner will soon be ready.
